subproblem.title: Continuous functions are bounded and integrable on the open unit cube
subproblem.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, let Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) carry Lebesgue measure (volume), and let Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. If f : Euclid k → ℝ is continuous, then (a) there is M ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ M for every y ∈ Q₁, and (b) f is integrable on Q₁.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), Continuous f → (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ y ∈ {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |f y| ≤ M) ∧ IntegrableOn f {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_bv_trace ("DG is continuous … so div G is continuous; it is therefore bounded on the compact set [0, 1]ⁿ ⊇ Q₁: |div G| ≤ M on Q₁") and step 1 ("Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ; so v_k … integrable on Q_δ"). Both uses are isolated here for an arbitrary continuous f : Euclid k → ℝ. The parent applies it with k = m + 1 to f = div G (part (a) gives its bound M) and to f = v_k (part (b), then restricted to Q_δ ⊆ Q₁).

Notation. Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Lebesgue measure `volume`; y_i is the i-th coordinate of y (in Lean `y i`, i.e. `WithLp.ofLp y i`). Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. K := {y : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i} is the closed unit cube.

1. K is compact. The coordinate map y ↦ (y_i)_i, i.e. WithLp.ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ), is a homeomorphism (Mathlib `PiLp.homeomorph 2 (fun _ : Fin k => ℝ)`, whose underlying map is WithLp.ofLp). A point y lies in K iff (y_i)_i lies in the box B := ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} [0, 1] = `Set.univ.pi (fun _ => Set.Icc 0 1)`, so K is the preimage of B under this homeomorphism. B is compact, being a finite product of the compact intervals [0, 1] (`isCompact_univ_pi` with `isCompact_Icc`), and the preimage of a compact set under a homeomorphism is compact (`Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage`). Hence K is compact. (For k = 0 the space Euclid 0 is a single point and the same argument applies verbatim.)

2. Q₁ ⊆ K, because 0 < y_i < 1 implies 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i.

3. Proof of (a). f is continuous, hence continuous on the compact set K, so it is bounded there: there is C ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| = ‖f(y)‖ ≤ C for every y ∈ K (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`). By step 2 the same bound holds for every y ∈ Q₁, so M := C satisfies |f(y)| ≤ M for all y ∈ Q₁.

4. Proof of (b). Lebesgue measure on Euclid k is an additive Haar measure, hence finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), and Euclid k is a Hausdorff space carrying its Borel σ-algebra. A function continuous on a compact set is therefore integrable on it (`ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact`: it is a.e.-strongly measurable for volume⌞K and bounded by C on a set of finite measure). So f is integrable on K, and integrability on a set passes to every subset (`IntegrableOn.mono_set`); by step 2, f is integrable on Q₁. ∎

subproblem.title: Set integrals over the shrunken cubes Q_δ converge to the integral over Q₁ as δ ↓ 0
subproblem.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Lebesgue measure (volume), Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and, for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {z : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}. If f : Euclid k → ℝ is integrable on Q₁, then ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺ (i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), IntegrableOn f {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → Tendsto (fun δ : ℝ => ∫ y in {z : Euclid k | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, f y) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ y in {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, f y))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_bv_trace ("Limit δ ↓ 0. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 4) ∈ (0, 1/4], δ_j ↓ 0; every point of Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. The functions 1_{Q_{δ_j}}w div G converge pointwise on Q₁ to w div G and are dominated by M|w|, which is integrable on Q₁. By dominated convergence, ∫_{Q_{δ_j}} w div G → ∫_{Q₁} w div G"), stated for an arbitrary f integrable on Q₁ (dominated by |f|; for f = w div G one has |f| ≤ M|w| on Q₁) and along the filter δ → 0⁺ (𝓝[>] 0), of which the parent's sequence δ_j = 1/(j + 4) → 0⁺ is a special case. The parent applies it with k = m + 1 and f = w · div G.

Notation. Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Lebesgue measure `volume`; y_i is the i-th coordinate of y (in Lean `y i`, i.e. `WithLp.ofLp y i`). Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. For δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {z : δ < z_i < 1 − δ for all i}; 1_E is the indicator function of E.

1. Openness and measurability. For a, b ∈ ℝ, {z : a < z_i < b for all i} = ⋂_{i ∈ Fin k} ({z : a < z_i} ∩ {z : z_i < b}). Each coordinate map z ↦ z_i is continuous (the continuous map WithLp.ofLp, `PiLp.continuous_ofLp`, followed by evaluation at i, `continuous_apply`), so each set {z : a < z_i} and {z : z_i < b} is open (`isOpen_lt`), and a finite intersection of open sets is open (`isOpen_iInter_of_finite`). Hence Q₁ (a = 0, b = 1) and every Q_δ (a = δ, b = 1 − δ) are open, in particular Borel measurable (`IsOpen.measurableSet`).

2. Inclusion. If δ ≥ 0 then Q_δ ⊆ Q₁: from δ < z_i < 1 − δ we get 0 ≤ δ < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ ≤ 1.

3. Reduction to the fixed measure μ := volume⌞Q₁. Put F_δ := 1_{Q_δ} f. For δ > 0, since Q_δ is measurable (step 1) and Q₁ ∩ Q_δ = Q_δ (step 2), ∫_{Q₁} F_δ = ∫_{Q₁ ∩ Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q_δ} f (`setIntegral_indicator`). The set (0, ∞) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (`self_mem_nhdsWithin`), so δ ↦ ∫_{Q₁} F_δ and δ ↦ ∫_{Q_δ} f agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and it suffices (`Tendsto.congr'`) to prove ∫_{Q₁} F_δ → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺.

4. Dominated convergence. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is countably generated (ℝ is first countable), so the dominated convergence theorem for countably generated filters (`tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence`) applies to μ, the functions F_δ, the limit f and the bound |f|:
 (a) every F_δ is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ, because f is (it is integrable on Q₁) and Q_δ is measurable (step 1);
 (b) |F_δ(y)| ≤ |f(y)| for every y and every δ (`norm_indicator_le_norm_self`);
 (c) |f| is μ-integrable, because f is integrable on Q₁;
 (d) for μ-a.e. y — it suffices to treat every y ∈ Q₁, because Q₁ is measurable (`ae_restrict_mem`) — F_δ(y) → f(y) as δ → 0⁺. Indeed, fix y ∈ Q₁ and i ∈ Fin k. Since 0 < y_i and 0 < 1 − y_i, every δ in a neighbourhood of 0 satisfies δ < y_i and δ < 1 − y_i (`eventually_lt_nhds`), i.e. δ < y_i < 1 − δ. Fin k is finite, so these finitely many eventualities hold simultaneously (`Filter.eventually_all`): y ∈ Q_δ for all δ near 0, hence eventually along 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0 (`nhdsWithin_le_nhds`). For such δ, F_δ(y) = f(y) (`Set.indicator_of_mem`), so δ ↦ F_δ(y) is eventually equal to the constant f(y) and converges to f(y).
Dominated convergence gives ∫_{Q₁} F_δ → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺, and by step 3, ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺. ∎ (Degenerate cases: for k = 0 the index type Fin 0 is empty, so Q_δ = Q₁ = Euclid 0 for every δ and the argument applies verbatim, `Filter.eventually_all` over an empty index being trivially true; for δ ≥ 1/2 the set Q_δ is empty when k ≥ 1, which is harmless because only δ → 0⁺ matters.)

Every y ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_δ for all sufficiently small δ (finitely many coordinates; Filter.eventually_all), so 1_{Q_δ} f → f pointwise on Q₁.
Dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0 with integrable bound |f| gives ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f.

subproblem.title: An affine bound in ∫|v_k| passes to the L¹ limit against a bounded multiplier
subproblem.statement: Let (α, μ) be a measure space (α : Type with a σ-algebra), S ⊆ α a measurable set, v_k : α → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ), w, h : α → ℝ, and A, B, M ∈ ℝ with B ≥ 0. Assume: every v_k and w are integrable on S; h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ restricted to S; |h(x)| ≤ M for every x ∈ S; ∫_S |v_k − w| dμ → 0 as k → ∞; and |∫_S v_k h dμ| ≤ A + B ∫_S |v_k| dμ for every k. Then |∫_S w h dμ| ≤ A + B ∫_S |w| dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (S : Set α) (v : ℕ → α → ℝ) (w h : α → ℝ) (A B M : ℝ), MeasurableSet S → 0 ≤ B → (∀ k, IntegrableOn (v k) S μ) → IntegrableOn w S μ → AEStronglyMeasurable h (μ.restrict S) → (∀ x ∈ S, |h x| ≤ M) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ k, |∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |v k x| ∂μ) → |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_bv_trace ("Limit k → ∞. |∫_{Q_δ} v_k div G − ∫_{Q_δ} w div G| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w||div G| ≤ Mε_k → 0, and |∫_{Q_δ}|v_k| − ∫_{Q_δ}|w|| ≤ ε_k → 0. Passing to the limit in the inequality of step 1"), stated for an arbitrary measure space (α, μ) with α : Type, a measurable set S, a multiplier h and constants A, B ≥ 0, M. The parent applies it with α = Euclid (m + 1), μ = volume, S = Q_δ (open, hence measurable), h = div G, A = (2(m + 1) + 1)V, B = 4(m + 1) and the bound M of its step 0.

Notation. ∫_S F means ∫ x in S, F x ∂μ, the Bochner integral for the restricted measure μ⌞S. Put ε_k := ∫_S |v_k − w|.

1. A.e. bound and integrability of the products. S is measurable, so μ⌞S-almost every x lies in S (`ae_restrict_mem`); hence ‖h(x)‖ = |h(x)| ≤ M for μ⌞S-a.e. x. Since h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞S and essentially bounded by M there, while w and every v_k are μ⌞S-integrable, the products w·h and v_k·h are μ⌞S-integrable (`Integrable.mul_bdd`: integrable times essentially bounded a.e.-strongly measurable is integrable). Also v_k − w, |v_k − w|, |v_k| and |w| are μ⌞S-integrable.

2. Difference estimate. Fix k. By linearity (step 1), ∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h = ∫_S (w h − v_k h), hence |∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S |w h − v_k h| (`abs_integral_le_integral_abs`). For every x ∈ S, hence for μ⌞S-a.e. x, |w(x)h(x) − v_k(x)h(x)| = |v_k(x) − w(x)|·|h(x)| ≤ |v_k(x) − w(x)|·M = M|v_k(x) − w(x)|, using |h(x)| ≤ M and |v_k(x) − w(x)| ≥ 0 (no sign condition on M is needed). Both sides are μ⌞S-integrable, so monotonicity of the integral (`integral_mono_ae`) and `integral_const_mul` give |∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S M|v_k − w| = M ε_k.

3. Comparison of ∫|v_k| with ∫|w|. For every x, |v_k(x)| = |w(x) + (v_k(x) − w(x))| ≤ |w(x)| + |v_k(x) − w(x)|. The three functions are μ⌞S-integrable, so `integral_mono` and `integral_add` give ∫_S |v_k| ≤ ∫_S |w| + ε_k.

4. Estimate for fixed k. By |a| ≤ |b| + |a − b| (from `abs_sub_abs_le_abs_sub`), the hypothesis for v_k, step 2, and step 3 multiplied by B ≥ 0:
|∫_S w h| ≤ |∫_S v_k h| + |∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ (A + B∫_S |v_k|) + M ε_k ≤ A + B(∫_S |w| + ε_k) + M ε_k = A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k.

5. Limit. Since ε_k → 0, the sequence A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k tends to A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M)·0 = A + B∫_S |w| (`tendsto_const_nhds.add (Tendsto.const_mul …)`). By step 4 the constant |∫_S w h| is ≤ every term of this sequence, so it is ≤ its limit (`ge_of_tendsto'`): |∫_S w h| ≤ A + B∫_S |w|. ∎ (Degenerate cases need no separate treatment: if S is empty or μ-null, every integral over S vanishes, the hypothesis for any k reads 0 ≤ A, and steps 1–5 still apply verbatim; likewise nothing above uses the sign of M.)

theorem Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_bvt_l1_limit : ∀ {α : Type} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (S : Set α) (v : ℕ → α → ℝ) (w h : α → ℝ) (A B M : ℝ), MeasurableSet S → 0 ≤ B → (∀ k, IntegrableOn (v k) S μ) → IntegrableOn w S μ → AEStronglyMeasurable h (μ.restrict S) → (∀ x ∈ S, |h x| ≤ M) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ k, |∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |v k x| ∂μ) → |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ| ≤ A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ := by
  intro α _ μ S v w h A B M hS hB hv hw hh hM hlim hbound
  have hae : ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict S), ‖h x‖ ≤ M := by
    filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem hS] with x hx
    simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hM x hx
  have hwh : Integrable (fun x => w x * h x) (μ.restrict S) := Integrable.mul_bdd hw hh hae
  have hvh : ∀ k, Integrable (fun x => v k x * h x) (μ.restrict S) :=
    fun k => Integrable.mul_bdd (hv k) hh hae
  have key : ∀ k, |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ| ≤
      A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + (B + M) * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := by
    intro k
    have hdiff : Integrable (fun x => |v k x - w x|) (μ.restrict S) := ((hv k).sub hw).abs
    have h1 : |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ - ∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| ≤
        M * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := by
      rw [← integral_sub hwh (hvh k), ← integral_const_mul]
      refine (abs_integral_le_integral_abs).trans (integral_mono_ae (hwh.sub (hvh k)).abs
        (hdiff.const_mul M) ?_)
      filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem hS] with x hx
      have hx' : |h x| ≤ M := hM x hx
      calc |w x * h x - v k x * h x| = |v k x - w x| * |h x| := by
            rw [← sub_mul, abs_mul, abs_sub_comm]
        _ ≤ |v k x - w x| * M := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx' (abs_nonneg _)
        _ = M * |v k x - w x| := mul_comm _ _
    have h2 : ∫ x in S, |v k x| ∂μ ≤ ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := by
      rw [← integral_add hw.abs hdiff]
      refine integral_mono (hv k).abs (hw.abs.add hdiff) fun x => ?_
      have := abs_add_le (w x) (v k x - w x)
      simp only [add_sub_cancel] at this
      exact this
    have h3 := hbound k
    calc |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ|
        ≤ |∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| + |∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ - ∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ| := by
          linarith [abs_sub_abs_le_abs_sub (∫ x in S, w x * h x ∂μ) (∫ x in S, v k x * h x ∂μ)]
      _ ≤ (A + B * ∫ x in S, |v k x| ∂μ) + M * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := add_le_add h3 h1
      _ ≤ (A + B * (∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ)) +
            M * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := by gcongr
      _ = A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + (B + M) * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ := by ring
  have hlim' : Tendsto (fun k => A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + (B + M) * ∫ x in S, |v k x - w x| ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (A + B * ∫ x in S, |w x| ∂μ + (B + M) * 0)) :=
    tendsto_const_nhds.add (hlim.const_mul _)
  simpa using ge_of_tendsto' hlim' key

proof_key_steps: |h| ≤ M on the measurable set S gives an a.e. bound for μ⌞S, so w·h and every v_k·h are integrable on S (Integrable.mul_bdd).
|∫_S w h − ∫_S v_k h| ≤ ∫_S |v_k − w||h| ≤ M ε_k with ε_k := ∫_S |v_k − w|.
Hence |∫_S w h| ≤ A + B∫_S |w| + (B + M) ε_k for every k (B ≥ 0).
Let k → ∞ (ε_k → 0) and conclude with ge_of_tendsto'.
